kinds.d: Card issued by a business to advertise it; a card issued in a numbered series to be collected is in Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards.

x.d: Engraved card of a Paris, Lyon or London shop, combining advertisement and directions before street numbering.
x.dt: trade · town · engraver or artist · paper

x.d: Colour-lithographed picture card sold blank on one side for any business to overprint its name.
Chromolithographed prints given to families by the Paris department store, imitated by its rivals.

kinds.d: Single printed advertising item kept after use, such as a handbill, flyer, leaflet or detached magazine or newspaper advertisement page; a poster is in Art, a catalogue or booklet in Media & Publications.
Large single sheet printed on one side, issued as a public notice, ballad or announcement.

x.d: Cheap single sheet printed with a topical song, sold in the street.
Sheet sold at British public executions giving an account of the crime, trial and often a confession.
Official announcement printed as a sheet for posting.

v.d: first printing of the US Declaration of Independence, about 200 copies

kinds.d: Printed or written receipt or billhead, kept.

x.d: Business invoice-receipt with a printed heading, often an ornate steel engraving of the premises.
x.dt: town or region · trade · illustration type · handwritten entries

brands.d: Paris department store developed by Aristide Boucicaut, an early issuer of chromolithographed advertising cards.

notes: All four old kinds kept. Liebig and tobacco series cards left to Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards. No named stock-card printer confirmed on a fetched page, so issuers stay as detail. Handbill kept with types only.
